name: Overcharger
body:
Artifice is not an exact science, at least not with current understanding. Overchargers are living manifestations of this fact, defying the normal limits of technology by raw force of will and pushing equipment well beyond normal limits. Even a single overcharger armed with only rudimentary equipment can pose a threat to the best-armed opposition due to their uncanny ability.

Gear Surge (Su)

The overcharger gains the ability to amplify the capacity of equipment in a variety of ways. As a free action, the overcharger may apply one of the following bonuses to a piece of equipment she is using until the start of the overcharger’s next turn. A piece of equipment cannot be affected by more than one instance of gear surge at a time.

The item’s granted enhancement or deflection bonus to AC, to natural armor, or on attack and damage rolls increases by 1.
The item’s granted resistance, luck, or morale bonus on saving throws increases by 1.
The saving throw DCs and skill check DCs needed to resist the item’s effects increase by 1.
The item’s caster level or manifester level increases by 1.

At 7th level and every 8 levels thereafter, the benefits of this ability increase by an additional 1.

Every time that an overcharger uses her gear surge ability, she has a 15% chance of suffering the effects of psychic enervation (as a normal wilder). For the purpose of prerequisites, effects of feats, and other class features, gear surge is treated as the normal wilder’s wild surge ability.

This ability replaces wild surge.

Surge Bond

In addition to the normal list of surge bonds, an overcharger may select from the following surges: armsmaster surge

Gear Surge and Psychic Enervation

An armsmaster overcharger specializes in channeling her abilities through weapons and armor. The armsmaster overcharger gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls with weapons affected by her gear surge and ignores any armor check penalties or movement speed reduction for armor or shields affected by her gear surge which she is proficient with. This bonus increases by 1 at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter. When an armsmaster overcharger suffers psychic enervation, she loses a number of power points equal to her manifester level and is staggered until the end of her next turn.

Surge Bond

An armsmaster overcharger gains proficiency with medium and heavy armor, martial weapons, and a single weapon of her choice. She may choose “firearms” or “heavy weapons” as the type of weapon she is proficient with.

Improved Surge Bond

At 5th level, when an armsmaster overcharger uses her gear surge on a weapon she is wielding, she may apply a weapon special ability with an enhancement bonus of +1 which can be applied to a soulknife’s mind blade to the weapon for the duration of the gear surge. When an armsmaster charger uses her gear surge on a suit of armor or a shield she is wearing, she may apply an armor special ability with an enhancement bonus of +1 which can be applied to an armored blade or shielded blade’s mind armament or mind shield for the duration of the gear surge. This enhancement bonus increases by +1 at 9th level and every 4 levels thereafter and may be divided between multiple enhancements (for example, a 9th-level wilder could use gear surge to apply the flaming and keen special abilities to her greatsword or the holy special ability to her greatsword).

Malfunction Surge

Gear Surge and Psychic Enervation: A malfunction overcharger’s abilities have the unique effect of tampering with machinery. When a malfunction overcharger uses her surge, she may choose a magical or technological item within close range (25 feet + 5 feet per 2 overcharger levels). If the chosen item is magical, the overcharger attempts a dispel check against the item’s manifester level (DC is 11 + the item’s caster or manifester level), suppressing the item’s magical or psionic properties until the start of the overcharger’s next turn (as per dispel psionics, with a duration of 1 round) on a successful check. If the chosen item is technological, the item’s wielder must attempt a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the overcharger’s level + her Charisma modifier). On a failed saving throw, the item cannot use any abilities that require charges until the start of the overcharger’s next turn and immediately ends any of its effects which require charges. Unattended equipment automatically fails its save. An item cannot be targeted by malfunction surge more than once per round.

When the malfunction overcharger suffers psychic enervation, she loses a number of power points equal to her manifester level and all of her equipment is treated as if it had been affected by her malfunction surge.

Surge Bond

The overcharger gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against effects created by items.

Improved Surge Bond

At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the malfunction overcharger increases their bonus on saving throws against items by 1 and gains a +1 bonus on dispel checks attempted as part of a gear surge.

At 9th level and every 8 levels thereafter, the Fortitude saving throw DC of the malfunction overcharger’s gear surge increases by 1.

Pilot Surge
Gear Surge and Psychic Enervation

A pilot overcharger channels her abilities through a mech or vehicle to augment its capabilities. A pilot overcharger can use gear surge on her mech’s natural attacks. A pilot wilder overcome by psychic enervation is dazed until the end of her next turn and loses a number of power points equal to her manifester level.

Surge Bond and Improved Surge Bond

A pilot overcharger gains a bonded mech, treating her class level as her pilot level.

Lasting Power (Su)

Starting at 4th level, whenever an overcharger uses her gear surge ability, she may choose one piece of technological equipment she is carrying. For a number of rounds equal to the bonus granted by the gear surge, this piece of equipment does not lose charges when used. Nanite canisters and other specialized ammunition other than charges are consumed normally.

At 12th level and every 8 levels thereafter, the overcharger may select one additional piece of equipment to be affected by this ability.

This ability replaces surging euphoria.

Ultimate Surge

At 20th level, an overcharger may supercharge everything around her once per day.

This causes any number of items within 30 feet of the overcharger to be affected by the overcharger’s gear surge, which has its bonus increased by an additional +5. Attacks made with weapons under the effects of ultimate surge ignore all damage reduction, hardness, energy resistance, and even energy immunity that their targets may possess.

After one round, the overcharger is struck by psychic enervation afterwards without fail, except she suffers her associated condition (dazed, staggered, etc.) for 1d4 rounds and loses a number of power points or hit points (dependent on path) equal to her manifester level + 10.

The overcharger also takes 2 points of ability burn to every ability score.

This ability replaces perfect surge.
